claim_text: A milligrams-per-kilogram reconstruction of the Choi digest was calculated and not adopted as the paper's result. The methods say the sample was diluted with 25 mL of water, not made up to 25 mL. If V is taken as 25 mL and mass as 0.200 g, mg/kg = C(µg/L) × 0.125. Code ML, rayon only, 19,558.35 µg/L, reconstructs to 2,444.79 mg/kg. If the 8 mL of acid is kept and 25 mL of water is added, the factor is 0.165 and the same sheet is 3,227.13 mg/kg. Mercury was not digested.
quote_trace: Section 2.2: Approximately 0.2 g of sample was added into a PTFE vessel containing 7 mL of 70% HNO3 and 1 mL of 50% HF. The samples were then transferred and diluted with 25 mL of ASTM type 1 water. Table 5 ML Sb 19,558.35 µg/L, fiber Rayon.

claim_text: One baby powder bought in Ibadan, Nigeria (sample 7PP, ash 95.9%, moisture 0.36%) contained 468 mg/kg lead and 112,000 mg/kg zinc. Two other laboratories reported lead of 508.5 and 364.63 mg/kg for the same sample, so the lead magnitude is corroborated; the zinc was reported as 103,750.8 and 41,872.6 mg/kg.

A second Ibadan baby powder (8PP) was reported at 36.3 mg/kg cadmium. The inter-laboratory check gave 25 and 0.38 mg/kg for the same sample. The value is contested and is not a headline or limit-comparison figure.

claim_text: The government limits printed in this collection that reach baby lotions, oils, or powders are: Health Canada cosmetics guidance (lead 10, arsenic 3, cadmium 3, mercury 1, antimony 5 ppm, technically avoidable above); Health Canada topical natural health products (same five values); German BVL 2017 (cosmetics in general lead 2.0, cadmium 0.1, mercury 0.1, arsenic 0.5, antimony 0.5 mg/kg, orientation values); and Washington RCW 70A.560.020(2) (lead intentionally added, or at or above 1 ppm, prohibited). The talc raw-material specifications are 21 CFR 73.1550 (lead 20, arsenic 3 ppm in a 0.5 N HCl extract, talc for colouring drugs) and JECFA 2003 (lead 2 mg/kg, food-grade talc).
